reason: Code-only recheck of the base-to-current diff. My earlier hold on 75459adc stands as an honest report of that revision. (1) Pinned policy: identityReviewTransportMaxBytes rejects any absent policy, extra keys, a wrong schemaVersion, or maxBytes that is not an integer or is outside 1024 to 768 KiB. Preparation seals transportPolicy in the receipt. validatePreparedIdentityReviewArtifacts runs the same check before writing, and writePreparedIdentityReviewArtifacts calls it first. createIdentityReviewBundle recomputes the split from job.transportPolicy, not a later default, and still requires byte-identical part transports bound to the source-packet hash, so a mismatched policy cannot pass. A journal without a policy throws the explicit reconciliation error. A test reproduces a 2-part layout pinned at 768 KiB, and another shows the 256 KiB default rejects that layout. (2) Independence: assembleChapterIdentityReviewParts still requires each part's actual agent to equal its report's reviewer, and excludes packet.authorAgentIds for every part. Removing the single-reviewer rule lets parts run in separate conversations. createIdentityReviewBundle binds each capture's agentId to its own report's reviewer. assertCapturedIdentityReviewParts now excludes receipt.authorAgentIds per part instead of forcing equality with the aggregate reviewer. The aggregate must contribute a part (producers.has(actualReviewerAgentId)), and report.reviewer must equal actualReviewerAgentId. (3) Aggregate: job.parts.some(agentId===job.agentId && runId===job.runId) replaces the final-part-run rule. Because the assembled digest must equal the original report, whose reviewer is reports[0].reviewer, the named aggregate is a real contributor and run pair. (4) Tests cover: the exact UTF-8 byte boundary at the 256 KiB default and a one-byte-over oversized single case, nine-part native recording that preserves every producer, a 768 KiB pinned layout, missing-policy and invented-run rejection, preflight rejection without creating output, and full current-source validation with mixed producers that rejects an extractor in any part and a non-contributing aggregate. I found no concrete regression in evidence completeness (project() is unchanged), exact case coverage, receipt reuse, or publication flags (still dataQualified:false and published:false). Limitations: I did not run the 63 checks. Whether the host actually calls the preflight before model dispatch and copies the policy into the journal happens in host dispatch code that is not in the reviewed diff. I did not exhaustively reread every line of the unchanged validators within the time budget. Distinct runIds across parts are not enforced, which I note as unverified rather than as a defect. A smaller part limit does not prove lower compaction, cost, or throughput. This is not an approval of any source, chapter, identity, date, ebook, live publication, or one-hour run.
